title: Where the deal stands: just, already and yet
grammar: Present Perfect com just / already / yet (andamento do negócio)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Present Perfect com just, already e yet para dar o status de uma negociação. Isso é essencial para o comercial da Delta Ducon dizer a clientes de siderurgia e cimento o que já foi feito, o que acabou de acontecer e o que ainda falta numa proposta de baghouse ou scrubber.
intro: In sales you often report progress on a deal. Has the client signed the order yet? We have just sent the quote. We have already visited the plant.
Today we practise the Present Perfect with just, already and yet. These small words tell the customer exactly where the deal stands right now.
introAudio: Good morning. I have just spoken to the client about the baghouse proposal. We have already agreed on the scope, but the customer has not confirmed the price yet. Let us learn how to report the progress of a deal.
vocab: The client has just placed the order for two scrubbers.
The customer has already approved the technical scope.
They have not signed the contract yet.
We have just sent the revised quote.
The plant has already confirmed the delivery date.
The buyer has not replied to our email yet.
practice: The client has just placed the ______ for two scrubbers.
The engineers have already checked the design, so we can ______ it.
They have agreed on the scope, but they have not ______ the contract yet.
We have just decided to ______ the revised quote by email.
The plant manager has just called to ______ the delivery date.
The buyer has not sent a ______ to our proposal yet.
The steel plant has already increased its ______ this month.
I have just asked my team to ______ the updated proposal.

audio.title: Status of the baghouse deal
audio.text: Let me give you the status of the baghouse deal. We have already visited the cement plant and measured the ducts. I have just sent the client a full quote for the filter bags and the fans. The customer has not approved the budget yet, but they have already confirmed the flow rate we need. My manager has just called the buyer to discuss the deadline. We have not lost this deal, and we have already done most of the work.

readAloud: We have just sent the quote to the client.
The customer has already approved the scope.
They have not signed the contract yet.
I have just spoken to the buyer.
Have you confirmed the delivery date yet?
fill: We have just ___ the revised proposal (send).
The client has already ___ the technical scope (approve).
They have not ___ the contract yet (sign).
I have just ___ to the buyer on the phone (speak).
The plant has already ___ the delivery date (confirm).
The customer has not ___ to our email yet (reply).
We have just ___ the order for two scrubbers (receive).
My manager has already ___ the price with the client (discuss).
qa: Have you sent the quote yet?
Yes, I have just sent the quote.
Has the client approved the scope?
Yes, the client has already approved the scope.
Have they signed the contract yet?
No, they have not signed the contract yet.
What have you just done?
I have just spoken to the buyer about the deadline.
Have you confirmed the delivery date yet?
Not yet, but we have already agreed on the scope.
sentences: We have just sent the quote to the client.
The customer has already approved the scope.
They have not signed the contract yet.
I have just spoken to the buyer.
Have you confirmed the delivery date yet?
We have already visited the cement plant.
The client has just placed the order.
The buyer has not replied to our email yet.
grammarPoint: Present Perfect = have / has + particípio passado. just = algo que acabou de acontecer (We have just sent the quote. — Nós acabamos de enviar a cotação). already = algo já feito, antes do esperado (The client has already approved it. — O cliente já aprovou). yet = em perguntas e negativas, algo ainda esperado (They have not signed it yet. — Eles ainda não assinaram).
deepDive: just e already ficam entre have/has e o particípio: I have just sent, she has already approved. yet vai no fim da frase e só aparece em perguntas (Have you signed yet?) e negativas (We have not signed yet). Lembre dos particípios irregulares: send → sent, speak → spoken, receive → received (regular).
examples: We have just sent the proposal.
Nós acabamos de enviar a proposta.
The client has already approved the scope.
O cliente já aprovou o escopo.
They have not signed the order yet.
Eles ainda não assinaram o pedido.
I have just called the buyer.
Eu acabei de ligar para o comprador.
Have you confirmed the price yet?
Você já confirmou o preço?
We have already visited the plant.
Nós já visitamos a planta.
The customer has just placed the order.
O cliente acabou de fazer o pedido.
The manager has not replied yet.
O gerente ainda não respondeu.
mistakes: We have sent just the quote.
We have just sent the quote.
just fica entre have e o particípio.
They have signed the contract yet.
They have not signed the contract yet.
yet aparece em negativas ou perguntas, não em afirmativas.
The client has already approve the scope.
The client has already approved the scope.
Depois de has use o particípio (approved).
I have just spoke to the buyer.
I have just spoken to the buyer.
O particípio de speak é spoken, não spoke.
Have you already sent it yet?
Have you sent it yet?
Não use already e yet juntos; em pergunta use yet.
quick: The client has ___ approved the scope (already).
They have not signed the order ___.
I have just ___ to the buyer (speak).
Has the plant ___ the date yet (confirm)?

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now report exactly where a deal stands — what is just done, what is already done and what is still open. That keeps every client informed and confident.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue relatar exatamente onde está um negócio — o que acabou de ser feito, o que já está feito e o que ainda falta. Isso mantém todo cliente informado e confiante.

title: How long we have worked together: for and since
grammar: Present Perfect com for / since (duração do relacionamento)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Present Perfect com for e since para falar da duração de um relacionamento comercial. Isso ajuda o comercial da Delta Ducon a mostrar a clientes de siderurgia e cimento há quanto tempo a empresa os atende e há quanto tempo fornece baghouses e scrubbers com qualidade.
intro: A long relationship builds trust in sales. We have worked with this steel plant for ten years. We have supplied their filters since 2015.
Today we practise the Present Perfect with for and since. They help you show the client how long the partnership has lasted and how solid it is.
introAudio: Hello. We have supplied this cement group for more than twelve years. I have managed their account since 2019, so I know their plant very well. Let us learn to talk about how long a partnership has lasted.
vocab: We have had a strong partnership for many years.
I have managed this account since 2019.
We have supplied their filter bags for a decade.
The client has trusted our service since the first order.
Our customer base has grown since last year.
We have had a contract with this plant since 2015.
practice: We have had a strong ______ with this steel group for years.
We have promised to ______ the filter bags on time for a decade.
The client has shown great ______ in our service since the first order.
Our ______ has grown a lot since last year.
We have had a ______ with this plant since 2015.
This ______ has lasted for more than fifteen years.
We have served this key ______ since 2018.

audio.title: A long partnership
audio.text: I am proud of our relationship with this cement group. We have supplied their dust collectors for more than fifteen years. I have managed the account since 2020, and I have visited their plant many times. They have trusted our engineering since the very first project. We have not lost a single order since 2018, because we have always delivered on time. A partnership like this has real value for both sides.

readAloud: We have worked with this client for ten years.
I have managed this account since 2019.
They have trusted our service since the first order.
We have supplied their filters for a decade.
How long have you worked with this plant?
fill: We have supplied this plant ___ fifteen years.
They have ___ our service since the first project (trust).
We have ___ with this steel group for a decade (work).
Our team has ___ their filter bags since 2015 (supply).
The client has ___ from us for many years (buy).
We have not ___ an order since 2018 (lose).
I have ___ this customer for eight months now (know).
qa: How long have you worked with this client?
We have worked with this client for ten years.
Since when have you managed the account?
I have managed the account since 2019.
Have you supplied them for a long time?
Yes, we have supplied them for over a decade.
How long has the partnership lasted?
The partnership has lasted for fifteen years.
Since when have they trusted your service?
They have trusted our service since the first order.

a.label: a duration with 'for'
a.placeholder: We have worked with them for ...

b.label: a starting point with 'since'
b.placeholder: I have managed the account since ...

sentences: We have worked with this client for ten years.
I have managed this account since 2019.
They have trusted our service since the first order.
We have supplied their filters for a decade.
How long have you worked with this plant?
Our customer base has grown since last year.
We have had a contract with them since 2015.
They have bought scrubbers from us for many years.
grammarPoint: Present Perfect com for e since fala de algo que começou no passado e continua até agora. for = duração (for ten years, for a decade). since = ponto de início (since 2019, since the first order). We have worked with them for ten years. — Nós trabalhamos com eles há dez anos. I have managed the account since 2019. — Eu gerencio a conta desde 2019.
deepDive: Use for com um período de tempo: for two years, for six months, for a long time. Use since com um momento específico: since 2015, since Monday, since we met. Cuidado: em português dizemos "trabalho aqui há dez anos" no presente, mas em inglês a estrutura correta é Present Perfect: I have worked here for ten years, não I work here for ten years.
examples: We have worked together for ten years.
Nós trabalhamos juntos há dez anos.
I have managed the account since 2019.
Eu gerencio a conta desde 2019.
They have trusted us since the first order.
Eles confiam em nós desde o primeiro pedido.
We have supplied filters for a decade.
Nós fornecemos filtros há uma década.
Our sales have grown since last year.
Nossas vendas cresceram desde o ano passado.
He has worked in sales for eight years.
Ele trabalha em vendas há oito anos.
We have had this contract since 2015.
Nós temos este contrato desde 2015.
She has known the buyer for a long time.
Ela conhece o comprador há muito tempo.
mistakes: We have worked together since ten years.
We have worked together for ten years.
Duração usa for, não since.
I manage this account since 2019.
I have managed this account since 2019.
Use Present Perfect, não Present Simple, com since.
We have supplied them for 2015.
We have supplied them since 2015.
Um ano é um ponto de início: use since.
They have trusted us since a long time.
They have trusted us for a long time.
a long time é duração: use for.
We work with this client for ten years.
We have worked with this client for ten years.
Ação que continua até agora pede Present Perfect.
quick: We have supplied them ___ fifteen years.
They have ___ our service for years (trust).
We have ___ with this plant for a decade (work).
She has ___ the buyer for a long time (know).

celebrate.en: Excellent. You can now show a client how long the partnership has lasted — a powerful way to build trust and win the next order.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue mostrar ao cliente há quanto tempo a parceria dura — uma forma poderosa de gerar confiança e conquistar o próximo pedido.

title: Too much or enough? Talking about price and scope
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar too e enough com adjetivos e infinitivos para falar de preço, prazo e escopo. Isso é útil para o comercial da Delta Ducon negociar com clientes de siderurgia e cimento, dizendo quando um preço está alto demais ou quando o prazo é suficiente para instalar um scrubber.
intro: In a negotiation you weigh things up. This price is too high for the client. The deadline is not long enough. Is the budget big enough to include the fans?
Today we practise too and enough with adjectives and infinitives. They help you explain limits and conditions clearly during a price or scope discussion.
introAudio: Let me be honest with you. The first price was too high for your budget, and the deadline was too short to install everything. Now we have enough time to plan the work properly. Let us learn to talk about limits with too and enough.
vocab: The budget is not big enough for two scrubbers.
The imported filter is too expensive for this project.
The deadline is too tight to install everything.
The client cannot afford the full package.
The discount is big enough to close the deal.
The scope is too large to finish in one month.
practice: The ______ is not big enough for two scrubbers.
The imported filter is too ______ for this project.
The deadline is too ______ to install everything.
The client cannot ______ the full package right now.
The ______ is big enough to close the deal.
The ______ is too large to finish in one month.
The extra ______ was not high enough to win the order.
This ______ is too small to cover both fans.

audio.title: Is the offer good enough?
audio.text: The client said the first offer was too expensive for their budget. The scope was also too large to finish in one month, and the deadline was too tight for our team. So we changed the proposal. Now the price is low enough to fit the budget, and the deadline is long enough to install the baghouse with care. The discount is big enough to close the deal, and the plant is happy enough to sign.

readAloud: This price is too high for the client.
The deadline is not long enough.
The budget is big enough for one scrubber.
The scope is too large to finish in a month.
Is the discount good enough to close the deal?
fill: The imported filter is too ___ for this budget (expensive).
The deadline is not ___ enough to install everything (long).
The budget is ___ enough for one scrubber (big).
This price is too ___ for the client to accept (high).
The discount is good enough to ___ the deal (close).
The scope is too ___ to finish in a month (large).
We now have enough time to ___ the work well (plan).
The offer was not attractive enough to ___ the order (win).
qa: Is the price too high for the client?
Yes, the price is too high for their budget.
Is the deadline long enough?
No, the deadline is not long enough to install everything.
Is the budget big enough for two scrubbers?
No, the budget is only big enough for one.
Is the discount good enough to close the deal?
Yes, the discount is big enough to close the deal.
Why did you change the offer?
The first offer was too expensive for the client.

b.label: a condition with 'enough'
b.placeholder: The budget is big enough to ...

sentences: This price is too high for the client.
The deadline is not long enough.
The budget is big enough for one scrubber.
The scope is too large to finish in a month.
Is the discount good enough to close the deal?
The offer was too expensive for their budget.
We have enough time to plan the installation.
The proposal was not attractive enough to win the order.
grammarPoint: too + adjetivo = demais, um problema (too expensive = caro demais). enough vem depois do adjetivo (big enough = grande o suficiente). Depois pode vir to + verbo (infinitivo): too tight to install = apertado demais para instalar; long enough to finish = longo o suficiente para terminar. The price is too high. — O preço está alto demais. The budget is big enough. — O orçamento é grande o suficiente.
deepDive: Ordem correta: too vem ANTES do adjetivo (too expensive), enough vem DEPOIS do adjetivo (cheap enough). Com substantivo, enough vem antes: enough time, enough money. Para dizer para quem, use for: too expensive for the client. Para dizer para quê, use to + verbo: enough time to install, too tight to finish.
examples: The price is too high for us.
O preço está alto demais para nós.
The deadline is not long enough.
O prazo não é longo o suficiente.
The budget is big enough for one scrubber.
O orçamento é grande o suficiente para um scrubber.
The scope is too large to finish in a month.
O escopo é grande demais para terminar em um mês.
We have enough time to plan the work.
Nós temos tempo suficiente para planejar o trabalho.
The offer was too expensive for the client.
A oferta era cara demais para o cliente.
The discount is good enough to close the deal.
O desconto é bom o suficiente para fechar o negócio.
The team is experienced enough to handle it.
A equipe é experiente o suficiente para lidar com isso.
mistakes: The price is enough high.
The price is too high.
"Alto demais" é too high; enough não significa "demais".
The budget is enough big.
The budget is big enough.
enough vem depois do adjetivo: big enough.
The deadline is too much short.
The deadline is too short.
Antes de adjetivo use só too, não too much.
It is too expensive for close the deal.
It is too expensive to close the deal.
Depois use to + verbo, não for + verbo.
We have time enough to plan.
We have enough time to plan.
Antes de substantivo enough vem primeiro: enough time.
quick: This price is too ___ for the client (high).
The scope is too ___ to finish in a month (large).
The budget is big ___ for one scrubber.
The filter is too ___ for this budget (expensive).

celebrate.en: Great work. You can now explain limits on price, time and scope with precision — a key skill for every honest negotiation.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você consegue explicar limites de preço, prazo e escopo com precisão — uma habilidade essencial para toda negociação honesta.

title: Selling the benefit: so and such
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender as estruturas so … that e such … that para enfatizar benefícios. Isso é útil para o comercial da Delta Ducon destacar a clientes de siderurgia e cimento que um baghouse é tão eficiente que reduz a emissão, ou que é uma solução tão robusta que dura anos.
intro: In sales you want the client to feel the value. Our filter is so efficient that emissions drop by half. It is such a strong system that it lasts for years.
Today we practise so … that and such … that. They help you highlight a benefit and show its powerful result to the customer.
introAudio: Let me show you the real value. Our baghouse is so efficient that the plant meets every emission limit. It is such a reliable system that you almost forget it is there. Today we learn to emphasise benefits with so and such.
vocab: The filter is so efficient that emissions drop sharply.
It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
The baghouse is so robust that it lasts for years.
The emission is so low that the plant passes every test.
It gives such strong performance that the client is impressed.
The saving is so big that the system pays for itself.
practice: Our filter is so ______ that emissions drop by half.
It is such a ______ system that downtime is rare.
The baghouse is so ______ that it lasts for years.
The ______ is so low that the plant passes every test.
It gives such strong ______ that the client is impressed.
The ______ is so big that the system pays for itself.
It is such an ______ design that the plant cuts its costs.
The gas ______ is so low that no rival can match it.

audio.title: A benefit the client can feel
audio.text: This solution is so efficient that the plant cuts its emissions in half. It is such a robust baghouse that it runs for years with little maintenance. The performance is so strong that the customer meets every legal limit with ease. It is such a good investment that the saving pays for the system in two years. The client was so impressed that they signed the order the same week. That is such a clear benefit that no competitor can match it.

readAloud: Our filter is so efficient that emissions drop sharply.
It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
The baghouse is so robust that it lasts for years.
The saving is so big that the system pays for itself.
It is such a good deal that the client signed at once.
fill: Our filter is so ___ that emissions drop by half (efficient).
It is ___ a reliable system that downtime is rare (such).
The baghouse is ___ robust that it lasts for years (so).
The emission is so ___ that the plant passes every test (low).
It gives ___ strong performance that the client is impressed (such).
The saving is ___ big that the system pays for itself (so).
It was ___ a good deal that they signed at once (such).
The scrubber is ___ effective that the gas comes out clean (so).
qa: Why is your filter better?
It is so efficient that emissions drop by half.
Is the system reliable?
Yes, it is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
How robust is the baghouse?
It is so robust that it lasts for years.
Why did the client sign so fast?
It was such a good deal that they signed at once.
Does the plant meet the limits?
Yes, the performance is so strong that it passes every test.

a.label: a benefit with 'so ... that'
a.placeholder: The filter is so efficient that ...

b.label: a benefit with 'such ... that'
b.placeholder: It is such a reliable system that ...

sentences: Our filter is so efficient that emissions drop sharply.
It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
The baghouse is so robust that it lasts for years.
The saving is so big that the system pays for itself.
It is such a good deal that the client signed at once.
The performance is so strong that the plant passes every test.
It is such a clear benefit that no competitor can match it.
The gas comes out so clean that the plant meets every limit.
grammarPoint: so + adjetivo + that = tão ... que (The filter is so efficient that emissions drop. — O filtro é tão eficiente que as emissões caem). such + (a/an) + adjetivo + substantivo + that = um(a) ... tão ... que (It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare. — É um sistema tão confiável que a parada é rara). that introduz o resultado do benefício.
deepDive: Use so quando vem só um adjetivo: so efficient, so robust, so low. Use such quando vem um substantivo: such a reliable system, such strong performance. Com substantivo contável no singular, não esqueça o a/an: such a good deal. Com incontável ou plural, sem artigo: such strong performance, such good results. O that muitas vezes pode ser omitido na fala, mas mantenha-o para escrever com clareza.
examples: The filter is so efficient that emissions drop.
O filtro é tão eficiente que as emissões caem.
It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
É um sistema tão confiável que a parada é rara.
The baghouse is so robust that it lasts for years.
O baghouse é tão robusto que dura anos.
It was such a good deal that they signed at once.
Era um negócio tão bom que eles assinaram na hora.
The saving is so big that the system pays for itself.
A economia é tão grande que o sistema se paga.
It gives such strong performance that clients are impressed.
Ele entrega um desempenho tão forte que os clientes ficam impressionados.
The gas is so clean that the plant meets every limit.
O gás fica tão limpo que a planta cumpre todos os limites.
It is such a clear benefit that no rival matches it.
É um benefício tão claro que nenhum concorrente iguala.
mistakes: It is so efficient system that emissions drop.
It is such an efficient system that emissions drop.
Com substantivo (system) use such, não so.
It is such reliable that downtime is rare.
It is so reliable that downtime is rare.
Só com adjetivo (reliable) use so, não such.
It is such reliable system that downtime is rare.
It is such a reliable system that downtime is rare.
Falta o artigo a antes de reliable system.
The filter is so efficient as emissions drop.
The filter is so efficient that emissions drop.
O resultado vem com that, não as.
It was so a good deal that they signed.
It was such a good deal that they signed.
Com a + substantivo use such, não so.
quick: Our filter is ___ efficient that emissions drop.
It is ___ a reliable system that downtime is rare.
The baghouse is ___ robust that it lasts for years.
It was ___ a good deal that they signed at once.
The saving is ___ big that the system pays for itself.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now emphasise a benefit so clearly that the client feels its full value — exactly what closes a sale.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue enfatizar um benefício de forma tão clara que o cliente sente todo o seu valor — exatamente o que fecha uma venda.

title: Comparing performance: as ... as and adverbs
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender (not) as … as e advérbios comparativos para comparar desempenho. Isso é útil para o comercial da Delta Ducon mostrar a clientes de siderurgia e cimento que uma solução não é tão cara quanto a do concorrente, ou que um sistema opera mais silenciosamente e instala mais rapidamente.
intro: In sales you compare how things work. Our system is not as expensive as the competitor's. Our baghouse runs more quietly and installs more quickly.
Today we practise as … as, not as … as, and comparative adverbs. They help you compare performance fairly and honestly with the client.
introAudio: Let me compare the two systems for you. Our solution is not as expensive as the competitor's, and it works just as well. It also runs more quietly and cleans the gas more efficiently. Today we learn to compare performance with as as and with adverbs.
vocab: Our fan runs more quietly than the old one.
This system installs more quickly than the standard model.
The new filter cleans the gas more efficiently.
Our baghouse operates as reliably as any premium brand.
The client can maintain it more easily.
Our price is not as high as the competitor's.
practice: Our fan runs more ______ than the old one.
This system installs more ______ than the standard model.
The new filter cleans the gas more ______ than before.
Our baghouse operates as ______ as any premium brand.
The client can maintain the system more ______ than the imported one.
Our price is not ______ high ______ the competitor's.
The new fan runs more ______ than the previous one.
Our baghouse cleans the gas ______ well ______ the premium brand.

audio.title: A fair comparison of performance
audio.text: Let me give you a fair comparison. Our baghouse is not as expensive as the imported one, but it works just as well. The fan runs more quietly, so the shop floor is calmer. Our system installs more quickly, so the plant loses less time. It also cleans the gas more efficiently and needs maintenance less often. In short, our solution performs as reliably as the premium brand, but it does not cost as much.

readAloud: Our system is not as expensive as the competitor's.
The fan runs more quietly than the old one.
This solution installs more quickly.
It cleans the gas more efficiently.
Our baghouse works just as well as the premium brand.
fill: The fan runs more ___ than the old one (quiet).
This system installs more ___ than the standard model (quick).
The new filter cleans the gas more ___ (efficient).
Our baghouse operates as ___ as any premium brand (reliable).
The team can maintain it more ___ (easy).
Our price is not as ___ as the competitor's (high).
The system needs maintenance less ___ than before (often).
Our solution performs as ___ as the imported one (good).
qa: Is your system as expensive as the competitor's?
No, it is not as expensive as the competitor's.
Does it work as well as the premium brand?
Yes, it works just as well as the premium brand.
How does the fan run?
The fan runs more quietly than the old one.
Does it install faster?
Yes, it installs more quickly than the standard model.
Does it clean the gas well?
Yes, it cleans the gas more efficiently than before.

a.label: a comparison with 'not as ... as'
a.placeholder: Our system is not as expensive as ...

sentences: Our system is not as expensive as the competitor's.
The fan runs more quietly than the old one.
This solution installs more quickly.
It cleans the gas more efficiently.
Our baghouse works just as well as the premium brand.
The team can maintain the system more easily.
It needs maintenance less often than before.
Their solution is not as fast as ours.
grammarPoint: as + adjetivo/advérbio + as = tão ... quanto (as reliable as = tão confiável quanto). not as … as = não tão ... quanto (not as expensive as = não tão caro quanto). Advérbios comparativos: a maioria forma more + advérbio (more quietly, more efficiently); irregulares: well → better, fast → faster. The fan runs more quietly. — O ventilador funciona mais silenciosamente.
deepDive: Advérbio compara COMO uma ação acontece: runs quietly, installs quickly. A maioria dos advérbios terminados em -ly usa more no comparativo: more quietly, more efficiently, more easily. Mas alguns são iguais ao adjetivo: fast → faster, hard → harder. Irregular importante: well → better. Em as … as, use o advérbio ou adjetivo base no meio, sem -er: as reliably as (não as more reliably as).
examples: Our system is not as expensive as theirs.
Nosso sistema não é tão caro quanto o deles.
It works just as well as the premium brand.
Ele funciona tão bem quanto a marca premium.
